inputs.source: Employee question via SSO-authenticated chat session
Published HR policy documents, authored by the HR content team, two-person reviewed before publish

instructions.note: "Do not give legal advice" is a prompt instruction only; nothing structural prevents a sufficiently adversarial or ambiguous question from eliciting legal-advice-like output. Bounded severity because the domain (HR policy) and output channel (text reply to the requester) limit potential harm.

elements.name: Agent reply to the employee's chat session

controls.name: Two-person review before policy publication
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the HR publishing workflow outside the model; a stronger model cannot bypass a human review step it never participates in. Only insider collusion between both reviewers would defeat it, which is outside the forecast triggers this rubric tracks.

controls.name: Read-only credential scoped to the policy index
controls.decay_rationale: The agent cannot read or act on anything beyond the policy index regardless of model capability; this is enforced by the credential grant, not by model behavior.

controls.name: Reply bound to the authenticated requester's session
controls.decay_rationale: The recipient of every reply is fixed by the chat platform's session binding, not chosen by the model; a more capable model cannot redirect output to a different recipient.

controls.name: Chat client disables image rendering and auto link-fetch
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced client-side; closes covert-channel exfiltration via rendered markdown images or auto-fetched links regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Network-level egress denial, verified by pen test
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced at the network layer and independently verified; the agent has no path to reach any external destination regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: Model version pinned, change requires a ticket
controls.decay_rationale: Model upgrades cannot occur silently; a change ticket gates them, which is the watch signal for the model_upgrade trigger rather than a source of decay itself.

controls.name: SSO authentication of the requesting employee
controls.decay_rationale: Identity of the requester is established by the organization's SSO layer outside the model and the agent's own behavior.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: do not give legal advice
controls.decay_rationale: Relies entirely on the model choosing to follow the instruction; a more capable or adversarially prompted model could still produce legal-advice-like content.

controls.name: Tamper-evident audit log of queries and replies
controls.decay_rationale: Not present in the design. Would not decay with model capability once added, since it is enforced at the logging layer, not by the model.

controls.name: Rate / step limit on policy_search and chat replies
controls.decay_rationale: Not present in the design. A hard cap enforced outside the model would not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Content-integrity / instruction-stripping filter on retrieved policy text
controls.decay_rationale: Not present in the design. Even if added, a classifier-based filter would only partially resist obfuscated or multi-document injection payloads as model capability grows.

findings.title: Internally authored policy content reaches the chat reply with no structural content-integrity check (RAG/document poisoning potential)

attack_path.note: HR policy content, authored by the HR content team, two-person reviewed before publish
Agent reads the published policy index with a read-only, least-privilege credential
Retrieved policy text, and any instruction-like content embedded in it, is relayed to the requesting employee

threat_refs.name: Context Memory Poisoning via Vector Store Contamination

forecast.watch_signal: Chat client configuration changed to allow replies to recipients other than the original requester, or the agent's credential scope widened beyond read-only access to the policy index.

evidence.observation: Policy index content is authored by the HR content team and requires two-person review before publishing, which reduces but does not eliminate the chance of injected or erroneous instruction-like text entering a published document.
The system prompt instructs the agent to 'find the relevant policy and quote it,' so retrieved policy text is inserted directly into the agent's output with no stated check for embedded instructions.
The agent's credential is read-only and scoped to the policy index, and replies go only to the authenticated requester's own chat session, bounding the consequence of any manipulated reply.

recommendations.action: Add a per-session and per-day rate/step limit on policy_search invocations.
Add tamper-evident audit logging of each query, retrieved excerpt, and reply, tied to the employee's SSO identity.
Add a content-integrity / instruction-stripping filter on retrieved policy text before it enters the model context.
Add an explicit system-prompt rule to treat retrieved policy content strictly as reference text, never as instructions, as defense in depth alongside the structural filter.

findings.title: No attributable record of agent queries or replies

forecast.watch_signal: A new tool or capability that writes, deletes, executes, configures, spends, delegates, or sends data outside the organization is added without a corresponding attributable audit record.

evidence.observation: No logging, audit trail, or action-provenance mechanism is described for queries submitted or replies sent by the agent.

recommendations.action: Implement tamper-evident logging of each query and reply, tied to the authenticated employee's SSO identity and timestamp.

findings.title: No rate, spend, or step limit on policy_search / chat replies

forecast.watch_signal: Autonomy level raised beyond A3, or median steps/runtime per session increasing, without a corresponding explicit rate or step cap being configured.

evidence.observation: No per-session, per-day, or overall rate, spend, or step limit is described for policy_search invocations, and autonomy.max_unattended_steps / max_runtime_minutes are not stated anywhere in the artifacts.

recommendations.action: Configure and enforce an explicit per-session and per-day query limit, and set explicit max_unattended_steps / max_runtime_minutes values.

stride_coverage.rationale: Single-process agent behind the organization's SSO-authenticated chat client, with no peer agents or protocol connections declared; there is no second identity for this process to spoof or be spoofed by.

rating.rationale: Three present findings were identified. (1) Internally authored HR policy content, two-person reviewed before publish, flows through the read-only policy_search tool into the chat reply sent to the requesting employee; this is a write-class sink under the rubric and rates inherent moderate (I source x S2 sink). Residual drops to low because the reply is structurally bound to the original authenticated requester's session and the agent's credential is scoped to the policy index only -- both model-capability-independent controls. (2) No attributable audit log of agent queries/replies exists, and (3) no explicit rate, spend, or step limit is configured; both are capped at low per rubric 5a because every affected capability only reads and answers the authenticated requester. The section 4 autonomy step/runtime modifier was deliberately not applied to finding (1), despite max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes being undeclared, because the design is architecturally a single search-then-reply call with no loop, chaining, or spawn capability described in any artifact; the undeclared-limits gap itself is instead captured directly as finding (3), to avoid counting the same root cause twice. The forecast is driven by two distinct changes: removing the destination-binding or credential-scoping controls (trigger: control_removal or data_scope_expansion) would revert finding (1) from low back to its moderate inherent level; and adding any new, more consequential capability (write, delete, execute, spend, delegate, credential access, or egress) without first adding audit logging or rate limits (triggers: new_tool, data_scope_expansion, autonomy_increase) would make findings (2) and (3) materially worse. The single control whose decay moves the forecast most is the destination-bound reply restriction that keeps every answer confined to the original requester's own authenticated chat session.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (prompt.md, tools.json, runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior; whether egress is truly blocked in production, whether two-person review is consistently enforced, and whether the chat client's no-render/no-auto-fetch behavior holds under all conditions have not been independently verified by this assessment.

Explicit numeric values for autonomy.max_unattended_steps and autonomy.max_runtime_minutes are not stated in the artifacts. The assessor inferred a bounded, single-call architecture from the system prompt and single-tool manifest rather than mechanically applying the rubric's autonomy modifier for undeclared limits, and recorded the corresponding gap as its own property finding (finding.missing_rate_limit) instead of as an escalator on the path finding.

No MCP configuration, IaC, or source code was provided. Credential scope, maestro layer, and the absence of logging/rate limits are inferred from prose runtime notes rather than verified configuration, so confidence on several fields is medium rather than high.
